beats.title: Rosetta Stone Decree Remits Taxes
beats.description: A priestly decree carved in three scripts praised a young Egyptian king for cutting temple taxes and pardoning debts.
beats.note: Memphis decree dated 196 BCE; one source says 195

beats.title: Han Dynasty Counts Its People
beats.description: Imperial officials recorded households and individuals across China, the earliest census whose figures survive.

beats.title: Quirinius Census of Judea
beats.description: Roman governor Quirinius counted the people and property of a newly annexed province for taxation, as the Gospel story recalls.
beats.note: Josephus and most historians give 6 CE; Luke's chronology implies earlier

beats.title: England Pays the First Danegeld
beats.description: After a defeat by Viking raiders, an English king handed over silver to buy peace, then taxed his people to raise it.

beats.title: Domesday Book Compiled
beats.description: A Norman king sent commissioners across England to record every manor, plough and pig so he could assess what he was owed.

beats.title: Saladin Tithe Raised
beats.description: A levy of a tenth of income and movable goods was ordered across western Europe to fund a crusade.

beats.title: Magna Carta Limits Royal Taxes
beats.description: Rebel barons forced a king to agree that certain levies could not be imposed without the consent of the realm.

beats.title: Florence Orders the Catasto
beats.description: The Tuscan republic required every household to declare its assets, creating a vast property register to tax fairly.

beats.title: Charles I Levies Ship Money
beats.description: A king ruling without Parliament revived a coastal naval levy in peacetime, then widened it, sparking a bitter dispute over his powers.

beats.title: Window Tax Introduced in England
beats.description: Householders were taxed by the number of windows in their homes, leading many to brick them up.

beats.title: Peter the Great Taxes Beards
beats.description: A Russian tsar set out to Westernise his nobles by charging a fee for wearing a beard and issuing a token as proof of payment.

beats.title: Kangxi Freezes China's Land Tax
beats.description: A Qing emperor decreed that the tax quota would never be raised to account for future population growth.
beats.note: Freeze announced 1711, commonly dated by the 1712 edict

beats.title: Stamp Act Passed
beats.description: Parliament required printed paper in the American colonies to carry a tax stamp, provoking the cry of no taxation without representation.

beats.title: Townshend Duties Imposed
beats.description: Britain taxed glass, lead, paint, paper and tea imported into the American colonies to pay colonial officials.

beats.title: Tea Act Passed
beats.description: Parliament let a struggling trading company sell tea directly to the colonies, keeping a tax on it that angered colonists.
beats.note: The Act itself, not the Boston Tea Party

beats.title: First US Census
beats.description: Marshals on horseback counted the inhabitants of the young republic, as the Constitution required.

beats.title: Hamilton's Whiskey Excise
beats.description: The new US government taxed distilled spirits to pay off war debts, angering frontier farmers who made whiskey.

beats.title: Pitt Introduces Income Tax
beats.description: To fund war against Napoleonic France, Britain's prime minister taxed incomes for the first time.

beats.title: First British Census
beats.description: Britain counted its people nationwide for the first time, finding fewer than expected as war with France raged.

beats.title: Corn Laws Enacted
beats.description: Britain barred cheap imported grain until home prices rose, protecting landowners while pushing up the price of bread.

beats.title: Britain Scraps Its Income Tax
beats.description: Parliament voted down the wartime levy after Napoleon's final defeat, ending the tax for a generation.

beats.title: Peel Revives Income Tax
beats.description: A Conservative prime minister brought back the income tax in peacetime to make up for lowered tariffs.

beats.title: Corn Laws Repealed
beats.description: Britain scrapped its tariffs on imported grain after a famine in Ireland and years of campaigning, opening the path to free trade.

beats.title: Window Tax Repealed
beats.description: After long complaints that it taxed light and air, England and Wales finally abolished the levy on windows.

beats.title: US Levies First Federal Income Tax
beats.description: To fund a civil war, Congress taxed incomes for the first time in the nation's history.

beats.title: Hollerith Machines Tally Census
beats.description: Punched cards and electric tabulators processed the American count in a fraction of the previous time.

beats.title: Lloyd George's People's Budget
beats.description: A British chancellor proposed taxing land and high incomes to fund welfare, triggering a constitutional crisis with the Lords.

beats.title: National Insurance Act Passed
beats.description: Workers, employers and the state paid into a scheme covering sickness and unemployment benefits.

beats.title: 16th Amendment Allows Income Tax
beats.description: The US Constitution was amended so Congress could tax incomes without dividing the revenue among the states.

beats.title: Smoot-Hawley Tariff Signed
beats.description: The US raised duties on thousands of imports, and trading partners retaliated as the Depression deepened.

beats.title: Social Security Act Signed
beats.description: The US began taxing wages to fund pensions for retired workers.

beats.title: Pay-As-You-Go Withholding Begins
beats.description: American employers started deducting income tax straight from paychecks to fund a world war.

beats.title: GATT Cuts World Tariffs
beats.description: Twenty-three nations signed an agreement to lower trade duties, laying the groundwork for the World Trade Organization.

beats.title: France Introduces VAT
beats.description: A tax collected at each stage of production, charged only on value added, was launched and later spread worldwide.

beats.title: California Passes Proposition 13
beats.description: Voters capped property tax rates and required a supermajority for new taxes, inspiring a wave of tax revolts.

beats.title: US Tax Reform Act Signed
beats.description: A sweeping overhaul slashed top income tax rates and closed loopholes in the American code.

beats.title: Poll Tax Starts in Scotland
beats.description: A flat per-person local levy replaced property rates a year before England, soon nicknamed the poll tax.
beats.note: Scotland first, April 1989; England and Wales a year later

beats.title: NAFTA Takes Effect
beats.description: The US, Canada and Mexico began phasing out tariffs on most goods traded between them.

beats.title: China Abolishes Farm Tax
beats.description: After many centuries, farmers in the world's most populous country no longer paid tax on their harvests.

beats.title: Global Minimum Tax Deal Agreed
beats.description: More than 130 countries backed a deal setting a floor on corporate tax rates to curb profit shifting.
